chapter_summary: Proverbs 24 covers a wide range of wisdom: stay away from evil people, build your life with wisdom, help those in danger, do not gloat over your enemies, do not be lazy, and be honest in all your dealings. The chapter holds up the man who keeps getting up after falling as a picture of true righteousness — and closes with a warning about the ruin that comes from laziness and sleep. Wisdom here is practical, relational, and deeply connected to the character of God.
main_lesson: A righteous person falls down but always gets back up. Build your life with wisdom and stay far from evil.

memory_verse.kjv: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
memory_verse.little_bible: A good person falls down many times. But they always get back up. The wicked fall and do not rise.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 24 is a rich chapter covering multiple wisdom themes that are all deeply connected: the company we keep, how we build our lives, how we respond to enemies, how we handle laziness, and how we tell the truth. The central verse — verse 16 — is one of the most encouraging in all of Proverbs: righteousness is not about never failing, but about always rising again. This is a deeply freeing truth for children (and adults) who feel crushed by failure.

The most important thing to communicate to your child is this: a good person is not someone who never falls. A good person is someone who always gets back up. This reframes failure not as identity but as experience — something to rise from, not be defined by. This is consistent with the Gospel: God's people are not perfect, but they are persistent in returning to God.

For application, walk through verses 30-34 with your child as an object lesson. Ask them what their own 'garden' looks like — is there anything in their life that is getting overgrown and neglected because of laziness? Help them identify one area of their life that needs more diligent attention.

For deeper study, connect verse 12 to Romans 2:6 and verse 16 to Micah 7:8. The wisdom of Proverbs always points forward to the righteousness fully revealed in Christ.
application_for_children: This week, when you make a mistake or fall down, say out loud: 'A good person gets back up.' Then get up and try again. Ask God to help you rise.

verses.kjv: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
verses.little_bible: Do not wish you were like evil people. Do not want to be around them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not wish for what evil people have.
verses.meaning: Envy toward the wicked is dangerous — it pulls the heart toward what God hates. Solomon commands his son not only to avoid wicked people but to stop desiring their company or their apparent advantages.
verses.prayer: God, help me never wish I were like people who do wrong.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we not want to be around people who do wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children recognise when they are beginning to envy what the wrong crowd seems to have — popularity, freedom, possessions — and redirect that desire?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one friend who makes good choices. Tell them one thing you admire about them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child turning away from a shadowy group of figures, choosing a different bright path, gentle warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
verses.little_bible: Evil people spend their time planning harm. Their mouths are full of trouble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Evil people plan harm and talk mischief.
verses.meaning: The reason to avoid evil company is revealed: their inner life is devoted to destruction and their words are full of mischief. Being near them is not neutral — their hearts and lips are working in a harmful direction.
verses.prayer: God, keep my heart from planning wrong. Fill it with good things.
verses.discussion_question: What fills the heart of someone who keeps doing wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that bad behaviour begins in the heart — and cultivate the heart, not just the outward actions?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: what am I spending most of my thinking time on today? Is it good?
verses.illustration_prompt: A dark heart with destructive thoughts swirling inside it, contrasted with a bright open heart full of good plans, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
verses.little_bible: Wisdom builds a house. Good thinking makes it stand firm.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom builds. Understanding makes it last.
verses.meaning: Wisdom and understanding are the foundational building materials for a family and a life. Not money, not strength, not luck — wisdom is what builds something that lasts.
verses.prayer: God, help our family be built on wisdom and good thinking.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to build a home with wisdom?
verses.family_discussion: What are we building into our family — through our words, habits, and priorities — that will still be standing in twenty years?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that helps build up your family — a kind word, a helpful act, or a wise choice.
verses.illustration_prompt: A warm home being built with glowing golden blocks of wisdom and understanding, a family working together, watercolour style

verses.kjv: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
verses.little_bible: Knowledge fills a home with beautiful and good things. Every room is richer because of it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Knowledge fills a home with good and beautiful things.
verses.meaning: Continuing the building metaphor, knowledge is what fills the rooms of life with richness and beauty. The home built on wisdom is not empty — it overflows with good things that come from knowing God and His ways.
verses.prayer: God, fill our home with the riches that come from knowing You.
verses.discussion_question: What good things can knowledge bring into a home?
verses.family_discussion: What kind of knowledge are we filling our home with — is it the knowledge that produces real richness of relationship, character, and faith?
verses.do_it_today: Share one thing you have learned this week that was truly valuable. Put it on the table like a treasure.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright home with glowing rooms filled with beautiful, precious things — books, warmth, family, wisdom — watercolour style

verses.kjv: A wise man is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
verses.little_bible: A wise person is strong. The more you know, the stronger you become.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom makes you strong. Knowledge increases strength.
verses.meaning: Wisdom and knowledge are not opposed to strength — they are the truest form of it. True strength is not just physical power; it grows with wisdom and understanding.
verses.prayer: God, make me wise and strong through knowing You more.
verses.discussion_question: How can knowing and learning make someone stronger?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that their most important strength is not physical but wisdom-based — and invest in it accordingly?
verses.do_it_today: Learn one new thing today. Know that it is making you stronger in the way that matters most.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing tall and strong, holding a glowing book of wisdom, strength and light radiating from them, watercolour style

verses.kjv: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors there is safety.
verses.little_bible: Wise advice helps you face hard battles. Many good advisors keep you safe.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Seek wise advice. Many good counsellors bring safety.
verses.meaning: No one wins their important battles alone. Wise counsel before acting — especially in serious conflict — is essential. Having multiple wise voices is a safeguard against error and pride.
verses.prayer: God, help me always seek wise advice before doing hard things.
verses.discussion_question: Who do you go to for good advice when things are hard?
verses.family_discussion: Who are the trusted, wise voices in our family's life — and are we actually seeking their counsel in our important decisions?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one hard situation you face. Find one wise person and ask their advice before you act.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child surrounded by trusted advisors — parents, a teacher, a kind elder — all speaking wisdom into a difficult situation, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Wisdom is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
verses.little_bible: Wisdom is too high for a foolish person. They have nothing true to offer.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Fools have no wisdom to speak.
verses.meaning: The 'gate' in ancient Israel was where civic decisions were made — a place of serious counsel. The fool cannot contribute there because wisdom is beyond their reach. Pursuing wisdom is not just personal — it has public significance.
verses.prayer: God, help me seek wisdom so I have something true to give.
verses.discussion_question: Why can a foolish person not offer wisdom to others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate the kind of deep wisdom in our children that will give them genuine things to contribute in important moments — not just noise?
verses.do_it_today: Before speaking into something important today, ask: 'Do I have something true and wise to offer here?'
verses.illustration_prompt: Wisdom sitting high on a mountain, a foolish figure unable to climb, standing silently at the bottom, soft watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
verses.little_bible: Anyone who plans to do evil will be known as a troublemaker. That is their name.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Evil planners are known as troublemakers.
verses.meaning: Planning evil is not just a private matter — it shapes your reputation and your identity. The person who schemes harm becomes known as a troublemaker. What we plan in our hearts defines us publicly.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from planning any wrong. Let my plans be good.
verses.discussion_question: What does it say about a person who plans to hurt others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that their private intentions shape their public character — and that what we plan matters as much as what we do?
verses.do_it_today: Check your plans for today. Is there anything you planned that you would not want everyone to see? Change it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with dark plotting thoughts visible above their head, a label forming that says 'troublemaker', watercolour warning illustration

verses.kjv: The thought of foolishness is sin: and the scorner is an abomination to men.
verses.little_bible: Even thinking foolish thoughts is doing wrong. And someone who mocks and scorns is hated by people.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Foolish thoughts are sin. Mockers are hated.
verses.meaning: Sin begins in thought — foolishness planned or entertained in the mind is already morally wrong. The scorner (one who mocks wisdom and God) represents an advanced state of moral failure that others recognise and reject.
verses.prayer: God, guard my mind from foolish and wrong thoughts today.
verses.discussion_question: Did you know that wrong thoughts are already doing wrong? How does that change how you guard your mind?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that sin begins in the mind — and cultivate the habit of bringing their thoughts to God?
verses.do_it_today: When a wrong thought comes today, say: 'No. I choose to think about what is good.' Then think of something true and good.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child catching a dark thought bubble and replacing it with a bright good one, peace returning to their face, watercolour style

verses.kjv: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
verses.little_bible: If you give up when hard times come, your strength is very small. Hard times show what you are made of.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Giving up in hard times reveals small strength.
verses.meaning: Adversity is a test of genuine strength. The person who gives up under pressure reveals that their strength was not real — it was only surface-level. True strength persists through hardship.
verses.memory_phrase: Do not give up in hard times.
verses.prayer: God, make me strong so I do not give up when things are hard.
verses.discussion_question: What is one hard thing you did not give up on? How did you feel when you kept going?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate resilience and genuine strength in our children — not sheltering them from all hardship but helping them develop through it?
verses.do_it_today: Find one hard thing you have been avoiding. Take one small step into it today. That is real strength.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing firm in a storm, bent but not broken, light coming from within them, watercolour scene of perseverance

verses.kjv: If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;
verses.little_bible: If someone is in great danger and you do nothing, that is wrong. You must not look away.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not look away from those in danger.
verses.meaning: This verse commands action on behalf of those in mortal danger. Passive inaction when you have the power to help is itself a moral failure. God calls His people to be active defenders of the vulnerable.
verses.prayer: God, help me never look away from someone who needs help.
verses.discussion_question: What should you do if you see someone in danger or being hurt?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to speak up and act — not stand by passively — when they see someone being hurt or in danger?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: is there anyone around me who is struggling or in trouble? What is one thing I can do to help them?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child reaching out a hand to rescue another child in danger, brave and caring, warm rescue scene in watercolour

verses.kjv: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?
verses.little_bible: You cannot say, 'I did not know.' God knows your heart. He sees everything. He will repay everyone for what they have done.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God sees your heart. He will repay everyone fairly.
verses.meaning: The excuse of ignorance fails before God. He is the searcher of hearts — He knows what we knew, what we chose, and what we did or did not do. Ultimately, He will render to every person according to their works. This is a serious accountability passage.
verses.prayer: God, You see everything I do and know. Help me choose right always.
verses.discussion_question: Can we ever truly hide from God what we know or do? Why not?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children an honest, non-performative accountability — not behaving only when watched, but living as those who know God sees all?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing you have been pretending not to know. Bring it honestly to God in prayer right now.
verses.illustration_prompt: An open book with a heart visible on its pages, God's gentle all-seeing light reading every word, a child looking on with honest reverence, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: My son, eat thou honey, because it is good; and the honeycomb, which is sweet to thy taste:
verses.little_bible: My child, eat honey — it is good and it is sweet. Enjoy it!
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Eat honey — it is good and sweet.
verses.meaning: This verse begins a comparison between honey and wisdom. First, Solomon affirms the real goodness of honey — he is not about to make a dry analogy, but a rich one. Physical sweetness is real; it sets up what follows.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for making good and sweet things for us to enjoy.
verses.discussion_question: What is something sweet and good that you really enjoy? Who made it for you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children receive and enjoy good gifts from God with gratitude — without either guilt or greed?
verses.do_it_today: Enjoy something good and sweet today and say thank you to God for it out loud.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child tasting honey from a honeycomb, eyes wide with delight and gratitude, warm golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
verses.little_bible: Wisdom is just as sweet to your soul as honey is to your mouth. Find it and you will be rewarded. Your hope will not be taken away.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom is as sweet as honey to your soul.
verses.meaning: Wisdom is to the soul what honey is to the body — sweet, nourishing, and deeply satisfying. The promise is clear: those who find wisdom receive a real reward, and their hope is not disappointed. This is an encouragement to pursue wisdom wholeheartedly.
verses.memory_phrase: Wisdom is sweet to your soul.
verses.prayer: God, help me love wisdom as much as the sweetest thing I have ever tasted.
verses.discussion_question: How can wisdom feel sweet — even sweeter than your favourite food?
verses.family_discussion: How do we make the pursuit of wisdom genuinely desirable to our children — not a chore but a delight?
verses.do_it_today: Read one verse of Proverbs slowly. Let it sit in your soul like something sweet. Let it stay there.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding a glowing piece of wisdom that shines like golden honey, tasting its sweetness with a joyful soul, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
verses.little_bible: Do not plan an attack against a good person's home. Do not try to ruin their safe place.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not attack the home of the righteous.
verses.meaning: This is a direct command against plotting harm to the righteous — targeting their home, their rest, their place of safety. It implies that such plots do exist and must be resisted.
verses.prayer: God, protect the homes of good people. Keep them safe.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we protect, not harm, people who are doing what is right?
verses.family_discussion: How do we stand up for and protect good people when we see them being treated unfairly or targeted?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone who is doing right. Say or do something today that encourages and protects them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A warm home glowing with peace and safety, a protective light around it, a shadowy figure unable to approach, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
verses.little_bible: A good person falls down many times. But they always get back up. The wicked fall and do not rise.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people fall but always rise. Wicked people fall and stay down.
verses.meaning: This is one of Proverbs' most encouraging verses. Righteousness is not defined by the absence of failure — it is defined by the persistence of rising. Seven times represents completeness: even through every possible failure, the just person rises again. This stands in vivid contrast to the wicked, whose fall is permanent.
verses.prayer: God, when I fall, help me always get back up again.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that a good person gets back up every time they fall?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model for our children the truth that failure is not final — that the righteous life is defined by rising, not by never falling?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you gave up on after failing. Take one small step to get back up and try again today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child falling down on a path, then rising again and again with determined joy, the sun rising behind them each time, encouraging watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
verses.little_bible: Do not celebrate when your enemy falls. Do not let your heart be glad when they stumble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not celebrate when enemies fall.
verses.meaning: This is a counter-cultural command: natural human instinct is to feel satisfied when an enemy falls. But God forbids it. Gloating over an enemy's failure is a sign of pride and a lack of love — it is not wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, help me have a kind heart even toward people who hurt me.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we not be happy when someone who hurt us gets into trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children a heart that does not gloat — that remains humble and merciful even toward those who have wronged them?
verses.do_it_today: Is there someone you have been hoping would fail? Ask God to give you a kind heart toward them instead.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child watching another child stumble, turning away from the temptation to laugh, choosing a kind expression instead, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Lest the LORD see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
verses.little_bible: God will see if you gloat. It will not please Him. He may even stop punishing your enemy because of your pride.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God sees when we gloat and is not pleased.
verses.meaning: God is displeased by gloating over enemies. The remarkable consequence here is that God may redirect His justice — withdrawing His discipline of the wicked — if the person watching becomes proud about it. Pride can actually work against justice. God's purposes are not served by our gloating.
verses.memory_phrase: God sees pride in our hearts.
verses.prayer: God, search my heart for pride and take it away. I want to please You.
verses.discussion_question: How does God feel when we are proud about someone else's trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that their heart attitudes — not just their actions — are visible to God and matter deeply to Him?
verses.do_it_today: Before judging or celebrating someone's failure today, stop and ask: 'Is this pleasing to God?'
verses.illustration_prompt: God's gentle watching eye seeing a prideful child, a cloud of displeasure forming, the child humbling themselves in response, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;
verses.little_bible: Do not worry and fuss about evil people. Do not wish you had what they have.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not worry about evil people or envy them.
verses.meaning: Anxiety about the apparent success of the wicked is a natural but spiritually dangerous response. Solomon commands: stop fretting. Do not let the wicked rent space in your mind through worry or envy.
verses.prayer: God, help me keep my eyes on You and not on what wrong people seem to have.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we not worry about evil people who seem to be doing well?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children resist the comparison trap — especially when the wrong path seems to produce attractive results in the short term?
verses.do_it_today: Name one person you have been comparing yourself to. Look away from them. Look toward God instead.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child turning their gaze from a distracting shadowy figure toward a bright horizon where God's light shines, peaceful watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
verses.little_bible: Evil people will have no lasting reward. Their light will be put out like a candle.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Evil people's light will be put out.
verses.meaning: The reason not to envy the wicked is clear: their apparent success has no future. The image of a candle being extinguished is vivid — the light of the wicked ends suddenly and completely. There is no eternal reward for those who reject God.
verses.prayer: God, help me always remember that Your way is the only lasting way.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that the wicked person's candle will be put out?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children hold an eternal perspective — seeing beyond what is visible now to what lasts forever?
verses.do_it_today: Light a candle and watch it burn. Remember: God's light in us lasts forever. Wicked people's light does not.
verses.illustration_prompt: A single candle going out in darkness, representing the end of the wicked's way, contrasted with an eternal light that never dims, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:
verses.little_bible: My child, respect God and respect the king. Do not get caught up with people who rebel and cause trouble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Respect God and leaders. Avoid rebellious people.
verses.meaning: True wisdom involves respect for both divine authority (God) and human authority (the king). Those who constantly stir up change and rebellion are dangerous companions — wisdom keeps away from them.
verses.prayer: God, help me honour You and the people You put in authority over me.
verses.discussion_question: Who has God put in authority over you? How do you show them respect?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to honour both God's authority and legitimate human authority — while cultivating discernment about when authority is misused?
verses.do_it_today: Show genuine respect to one person in authority over you today. Not because you have to — because God says it is right.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child bowing respectfully before a kind king, God's light blessing both of them, a scene of rightful honour and peace, watercolour style

verses.kjv: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
verses.little_bible: Big trouble comes suddenly to those who rebel. No one knows how bad the ruin will be.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Rebellion brings sudden, unknown ruin.
verses.meaning: The ruin that falls on those who rebel against God and authority is sudden and unpredictable — no one can calculate how bad it will be. This unpredictability is itself part of the warning: the wise do not gamble with such danger.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from rebellion. I want to walk in Your safe way.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it risky to hang around people who do not respect God or leaders?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that the company they keep determines the dangers they face — and choose companions wisely?
verses.do_it_today: Think of the five people you spend the most time with. Are they moving you toward God or away from Him?
verses.illustration_prompt: A stormy sky breaking suddenly over a rebellious figure, shock and ruin arriving without warning, a wise child watching from a safe distance, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
verses.little_bible: Here is more wisdom. It is not right to treat people differently in a court of law. Every person must be judged fairly.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Every person must be judged fairly.
verses.meaning: Partiality in judgment — treating people differently based on who they are rather than what they did — is a serious failure of justice. True wisdom demands fairness for all, regardless of wealth, status, or connection.
verses.prayer: God, help me be fair to all people and never show partiality.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be fair to everyone — even people who are different from you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model and teach fairness in our family — equal treatment, consistent standards, and no favouritism?
verses.do_it_today: Is there someone you have been treating unfairly? Choose to treat them fairly today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A balanced scale with two equal sides, people of different appearances standing on each side in equal measure, calm watercolour justice scene

verses.kjv: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
verses.little_bible: Anyone who tells a wicked person that they are doing right will be cursed by people. Nations will hate them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Calling the wicked righteous brings a curse.
verses.meaning: False validation of wickedness — telling the wicked their ways are acceptable — is a profound moral failure. It brings widespread condemnation. People recognise this as an injustice even when they cannot articulate why: calling evil good is fundamentally wrong.
verses.prayer: God, help me never call wrong things right. Give me courage to be honest.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wrong to tell someone their bad behaviour is okay?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children be truthful and courageous when someone is doing wrong — not validating it to avoid conflict, but speaking honestly in love?
verses.do_it_today: Is there something in your life or someone around you that you have been calling okay when it is not? Be honest about it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure approving of a wicked act with a nod, others turning away from them in disapproval, a dark consequence forming, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
verses.little_bible: But those who correct the wicked will be delighted. A good blessing will come to them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honest correction brings blessing and delight.
verses.meaning: In direct contrast to verse 24, those who rebuke the wicked receive not condemnation but blessing. Honest correction — even when hard — is ultimately rewarded. People recognise truth-tellers and bless them.
verses.prayer: God, give me courage to correct with love and wisdom.
verses.discussion_question: Has someone's honest correction ever actually helped you? How did it feel later?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a family culture where honest correction is received as a gift rather than an attack — and where we give correction with love rather than harshness?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a time you were corrected and it helped you. Thank that person today if you can.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child gently correcting another child, both smiling with honesty and warmth, a golden blessing resting on the correcting child, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Every man shall kiss his lips that giveth a right answer.
verses.little_bible: A person who gives a true and right answer is deeply valued. Everyone loves a true word.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A true, right answer is deeply valued.
verses.meaning: The 'kiss on the lips' represents deep affection and honour. A person who gives a right, honest answer earns great respect — they are valued by all who receive the truth from them.
verses.prayer: God, help me always give true and right answers to those who ask me.
verses.discussion_question: Why is a true, honest answer so valuable to people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate the habit of truth-telling in our family — so that our words can be trusted completely?
verses.do_it_today: Give one completely honest answer today to a question someone asks — even if the truth is harder than a comfortable answer.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking a true word, another child's face lighting up with gratitude and affection, warmth and trust between them, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
verses.little_bible: First do your outside work. Get the field ready. Then build your house. Do things in the right order.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: First prepare your work, then build your house.
verses.meaning: Wisdom involves right ordering — doing the foundational preparatory work before building. Rushing to the visible goal without completing the necessary preparation leads to an unstable result.
verses.prayer: God, help me do things in the right order with wisdom and patience.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of something you need to prepare before you can build or start something bigger?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to prioritise preparation — doing the groundwork first before launching into their goals and dreams?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one big goal. Write down the three preparation steps that come before you can begin building it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child working diligently in a field before laying the foundation of a house, step-by-step wisdom visible in their actions, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive not with thy lips.
verses.little_bible: Do not speak against your neighbour without a real reason. Do not lie with your mouth.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Never speak against neighbours without cause or lie.
verses.meaning: False testimony and groundless accusation are serious wrongs. This verse commands both honesty and restraint — only speak against someone if there is a real and just reason, and never use deception.
verses.prayer: God, keep my mouth from saying anything false about the people around me.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wrong to say bad things about someone if they are not true?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to defend the reputation of others — not gossip, not accuse without cause, not spread stories they are not sure of?
verses.do_it_today: Before you say anything about someone else today, ask: 'Is this true? Is this kind? Is it necessary?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding their mouth closed, choosing not to speak against a neighbour without cause, a thoughtful and wise expression, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
verses.little_bible: Do not say, 'I will pay them back for what they did to me.' Leave justice to God. Do not take revenge.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not take revenge. Leave it to God.
verses.meaning: Revenge — the insistence on repaying hurt for hurt — is forbidden. The believer is commanded not to take personal justice into their own hands. This anticipates Romans 12:19: 'Vengeance is mine, saith the Lord.'
verses.prayer: God, help me not pay back wrong for wrong. You are the fair judge.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wrong to pay someone back when they have hurt you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to resist the natural instinct to retaliate — and trust God with the justice they feel they are owed?
verses.do_it_today: Is there someone who hurt you that you have wanted to pay back? Give that hurt to God in prayer today instead.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child choosing to walk away from a conflict instead of retaliating, peace on their face, God's light guiding them forward, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
verses.little_bible: One day I walked past the field of a lazy person. I saw the farm of a man with no wisdom.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: I walked past a lazy person's ruined field.
verses.meaning: The teacher speaks from personal observation — this is not theory but lived experience. He walked past the field of the lazy person and saw what laziness produces. The scene about to be described is a powerful warning.
verses.prayer: God, help me never let laziness ruin what You have given me.
verses.discussion_question: What do you think a lazy person's garden looks like? What happens when we do not take care of things?
verses.family_discussion: What in our family is at risk of being neglected and overgrown because of laziness or inattention? What needs care right now?
verses.do_it_today: Walk around your home or school. Find one thing that has been neglected. Take care of it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise person walking past an overgrown and neglected field, observing it with thoughtful sadness, warm afternoon watercolour scene

verses.kjv: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
verses.little_bible: The field was full of weeds and thorns. Nettles covered everything. The wall was broken down.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The neglected field was full of thorns and broken down.
verses.meaning: The picture of the neglected field is vivid and complete: thorns, nettles, a broken wall. Laziness does not simply produce nothing — it produces damage, ruin, and overgrowth. Neglect has real, tangible consequences.
verses.prayer: God, help me be faithful with the things You have given me to care for.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to a garden when nobody takes care of it? What does that teach us?
verses.family_discussion: What 'walls' in our family life have grown broken through neglect — relationships, habits, disciplines — that need to be rebuilt?
verses.do_it_today: Fix or care for one thing today that has been broken or neglected. Even a small repair matters.
verses.illustration_prompt: An overgrown field full of thorns and weeds, a broken stone wall, decay and ruin visible everywhere, a sad but instructive watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
verses.little_bible: I looked carefully at all of it. I thought hard about what I saw. And I learned from it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: I looked carefully and received instruction.
verses.meaning: The teacher models the response to observation: careful, considered reflection that becomes instruction. He does not just walk past — he stops, looks hard, and receives the lesson. This is wisdom's posture: learning from what is visible in the world.
verses.prayer: God, help me learn from what I see around me every day.
verses.discussion_question: What is one thing you have seen that taught you an important lesson?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to be active learners from their environment — seeing instruction in what happens around them, not just in formal lessons?
verses.do_it_today: Spend two minutes looking carefully at something around you. Ask: 'What is God teaching me through this?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise person kneeling down to look carefully at the neglected field, eyes thoughtful and open, receiving deep instruction, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
verses.little_bible: Just a little more sleep. Just a little more rest. Just folding my hands to sleep a bit longer.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A little more sleep... a little more rest...
verses.meaning: This verse quotes the lazy person's own inner monologue — each 'little' seems harmless in isolation, but together they describe a pattern of perpetual avoidance. The repetition of 'little' is the point: it is the smallness that makes it dangerous.
verses.prayer: God, help me not make excuses for laziness. Help me get up and work.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever said 'just a little more' about something and then kept putting things off? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: How do we recognise and address the small increments of laziness in our own lives — the 'just a little more' patterns that add up to real neglect?
verses.do_it_today: If you have been putting something off, do not say 'just a little later.' Do it now.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child curled up in bed saying 'just a little more sleep' as work waits undone outside the window, gentle warning watercolour scene

verses.kjv: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
verses.little_bible: Then poverty will come like a traveller walking toward you. Your need will come like a soldier ready to fight. You will not be able to stop it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Laziness brings poverty like an unstoppable soldier.
verses.meaning: The consequence of the lazy person's 'little by little' delays is devastating: poverty arrives unstoppably — like a traveller who keeps coming no matter what, or an armed soldier who cannot be resisted. Laziness is not a small thing; it produces real and serious ruin.
verses.prayer: God, protect me from laziness. Help me work faithfully every day.
verses.discussion_question: What happens at the end of the road for the person who keeps being lazy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we close this chapter as a family by asking honestly: where has laziness been creeping into our lives, and what do we need to do about it today?
verses.do_it_today: Name one area of your life where laziness has been building up. Make a specific plan to address it — starting today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A strong armoured soldier marching toward a sleeping figure, poverty arriving unavoidably, a sobering and powerful watercolour warning scene
